This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korova Coleman.
The National Hurricane Center says a tropical system in the Gulf of Mexico is now flourished
into Hurricane Isaias.

Lauren Linham is the environmental reporter for member station WBHM.
It's been a pretty quiet hurricane season so far with El Nino in place.
So, areas from the Mississippi Gulf Coast all the way to the Florida Panhandle, especially

This year's Nobel Prize for Literature will be announced this morning.
The winner of the renowned Nobel Peace Prize will be revealed tomorrow.
NPR's Emily Fang reports President Trump says he deserves the Peace Prize despite starting
an ongoing war with Iran.
Trump argues that he should be recognized for stopping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon.
I did things that nobody else has ever done.
I'm not bragging.
I'm just telling you the facts.
Trump has criticized the Nobel Prize committee in the past for giving former President Barack
Obama a peace prize, but not him.
He also said he'd "indirectly" won the prize after last year's recipient, Venezuelan
opposition activist Maria Corino Machado, gave Trump the award medal.
And she gave it to me and I said, "Wow, what an honor."
I settled eight wars.
Another one is coming.
Another war or another award, the president did not specify what he meant by that.
Emily Fang and Pure News, the White House.
The aircraft carrier, the USS Abraham Lincoln, returns to San Diego today after a deployment
of 321 days.
It's become a symbol of the war against Iran that's gone on longer than was expected.
Steve Futterman reports from San Diego.
What was supposed to be a six-month mission changed when the U.S. war with Iran began in
February.
It was a problem-filled deployment.
There were food and water shortages, difficulties with air conditioning and plumbing.
For some it was too much.
The Navy confirmed there were a number of suicide attempts.
Yesterday, Secretary of Defense Pete Hexeth flew out to meet the Lincoln.
He thanked the crew and criticized news reports of problems.
There were a few folks in the media who tried to turn the USS Abraham Lincoln into some
sort of a symbol, a symbol of dysfunction.
I know it's the exact opposite.
Hundreds of relatives are expected to be at the naval base to greet the crew.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in San Diego.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
President Trump attended a campaign rally in San Antonio, Texas yesterday to support
Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton.
Trump also faced protesters. At one point, he stepped away from the microphone after
a protester got close to the stage.
In Spain, an 87-year-old woman who had been evicted from her longtime apartment in Madrid
died yesterday in a hospital.
As NPR's Miguel Macias reports from Seville, her eviction sparked nationwide protests and
unleashed a political crisis in Spain.
It was only two weeks ago that activists tried to stop the eviction of Maritel Carmen Avascal.
The images of Maritel Carmen, as she's known, being taken to the hospital in an ambulance
went viral around the world.
What followed was a national crisis.
Thousands of protesters took to the streets, fed up with a deepening affordability crisis
in the rental market.
After trying and failing to pass a set of emergency measures, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced
snap elections on Monday morning, but on Wednesday, yet another shock.
Maritel Carmen had died in the hospital before she had a chance to sign a new contract to
return to her home.
Prime Minister Sanchez offered his condolences on social media, the head of the opposition
party did as well, adding that no party should make use of these for political purposes.
Miguel Macias, NPR News, Seville, Spain.
NASA says four astronauts aboard a SpaceX capsule are scheduled to splash down later
this morning off the California coast.
The crew's been aboard the International Space Station for nearly eight months.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.
